lessons.title: The right detail, not just a matching word
lessons.strategy: A longer text can hold several numbers, names or times. Use the whole question to find the right paragraph, then the one sentence that answers it.
lessons.tip: Before you answer, check that your detail matches every part of the question.

worked.prompt: How many books were on the shelf by Friday?
steps: The text has three numbers about books: twelve, four and forty-one.
The question says by Friday. Find Friday: 'By Friday, the shelf held forty-one books.'
Twelve was in June and four was on Monday. They are about books, but they do not answer this question. The answer is forty-one.

lessons.title: Follow the time words
lessons.strategy: Time words such as on Monday, then, by Friday, after that and finally show when each thing happened. Use them to put the events in order.
lessons.tip: Circle the time words in your head, then place the question's event among them.

worked.prompt: What happened after only four books came on Monday?
worked.answer: Farid made a chart with every child's name.
steps: Find the event: 'On Monday, only four books came.'
The next sentence begins with Then: 'Then Farid had an idea.' He made a chart.
The forty-one books came later, by Friday. So the next thing was Farid's chart.

lessons.title: The reason may be in another sentence
lessons.strategy: Writers do not always say because. Ask what changed just before the thing happened. The cause is often one or two sentences earlier.
lessons.tip: Try joining the two sentences with because. If it makes sense, you have found the cause.

worked.prompt: Why did the number of books grow so quickly by Friday?
worked.answer: Each child who brought a book got a green dot on Farid's chart.
steps: The effect is: 'By Friday, the shelf held forty-one books.' No because is given.
What changed just before? Farid's chart: 'Each time someone brought a book, they got a green dot.'
Join them: the shelf filled because children wanted a green dot beside their name. It makes sense, so that is the cause.

lessons.title: Why did they do that?
lessons.strategy: To find why someone acts, look at what they saw or what happened just before, and at what they did next. The reason links the two.
lessons.tip: Ask: what problem was this person trying to solve?

worked.prompt: Why did Farid make the chart?
worked.answer: He wanted more children to bring books.
steps: What happened just before? 'On Monday, only four books came.' That was the problem.
What did Farid do? He made a chart that gave a green dot to each child who brought a book.
The chart rewards bringing a book. So Farid wanted more children to bring books.

lessons.title: The big idea of a paragraph
lessons.strategy: Each paragraph has one big idea. The other sentences give details about it. Choose the idea that the other sentences support.
lessons.tip: If you could say 'for example' before it, it is a detail, not the main idea.

worked.prompt: What is the main idea of the last paragraph?
worked.answer: The children now look after the library themselves.
steps: Read the paragraph's first sentence: 'Now the children run the library themselves.'
The next sentence gives examples: two children stamp the cards, and there is a one-week rule.
Stamping cards is a detail that supports the first sentence. The main idea is that the children run the library.

lessons.title: Spot the opinion words
lessons.strategy: Opinions often carry signal words: I think, I believe, should, best, worst, most exciting. A fact gives something that can be checked, such as a number, a date or an event.
lessons.tip: Look for should, best and I think. Then ask whether everyone would have to agree.

worked.answer: I think it is the best corner of the school.
steps: 'By Friday, the shelf held forty-one books.' We could count them. It is a fact.
'I think it is the best corner of the school.' It has two signal words: I think and best.
Someone else might prefer the playground. It cannot be checked, so it is an opinion.

passages.title: The Class Library
passages.text:
Last June, Class 5B had only twelve storybooks, and most of them had torn covers. Their teacher, Mrs Rao, wanted the children to read more. She asked every child to bring one old book from home.

On Monday, only four books came. Then Farid had an idea. He made a chart with every child's name and stuck it near the door. Each time someone brought a book, they got a green dot. By Friday, the shelf held forty-one books.

Now the children run the library themselves. Two children stamp the cards at lunch, and nobody may keep a book for more than a week. I think it is the best corner of the school. Every class should have a library like this.

passages.title: The Steel Bottle Rule
passages.text:
Every summer, the playground at Hill View School was covered in plastic bottles. The gardener, Mr Das, filled three sacks with them every week. He was tired of it.

In April, the head teacher made a new rule. Children had to bring a steel bottle from home, and the shop inside the school stopped selling water in plastic bottles. At first, many children forgot. So the school put two big water tanks near the gate, where bottles could be filled.

After a month, Mr Das filled only half a sack a week. He started using his free time to plant a row of sunflowers along the wall. Steel bottles are the best answer to litter. I think every school should follow this rule.

questions.prompt: How many sacks did Mr Das fill each week before the new rule?
questions.right: three
wrong: half a sack
two
questions.evidence: filled three sacks with them every week
questions.explain: Before the rule he filled three sacks a week. Half a sack is from after the rule, and two is the number of water tanks.
questions.hint: Two numbers in the text are about sacks. Which one comes before the rule was made?

questions.prompt: What did the school do after many children forgot their bottles?
questions.right: It put two big water tanks near the gate.
wrong: It stopped selling water in plastic bottles.
It planted sunflowers along the wall.
questions.evidence: So the school put two big water tanks near the gate
questions.explain: 'At first, many children forgot. So the school put two big water tanks near the gate.' The shop had stopped selling plastic bottles earlier, and the sunflowers were Mr Das's work later.
questions.hint: Find 'At first, many children forgot.' The next sentence begins with So.

questions.prompt: Why did Mr Das have free time after a month?
questions.right: There were far fewer bottles to pick up.
wrong: The head teacher gave him two days off each week.
The sunflowers needed less water.
questions.evidence: After a month, Mr Das filled only half a sack a week.
questions.explain: He went from three sacks to half a sack a week. Less litter to collect left him free time. The text does not say because, but the two sentences link.
questions.hint: What changed about his sacks just before the sentence about free time?

questions.prompt: Why did the head teacher make the new rule?
questions.right: To cut the plastic litter on the playground.
wrong: To sell more steel bottles.
To give the gardener more work to do each week.
questions.evidence: the playground at Hill View School was covered in plastic bottles
questions.explain: The problem just before the rule was a playground covered in plastic bottles. The rule removes plastic bottles, so it was made to cut the litter.
questions.hint: What problem does the first paragraph describe? What does the rule take away?

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the last paragraph?
questions.right: The rule worked: there was much less litter.
wrong: Mr Das likes sunflowers.
There are two big water tanks near the school gate.
questions.evidence: After a month, Mr Das filled only half a sack a week.
questions.explain: The paragraph shows the result of the rule: only half a sack of litter. The sunflowers are a detail, and the tanks are in another paragraph.
questions.hint: What does the first sentence of that paragraph tell you? The rest supports it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Steel bottles are the best answer to litter.
wrong: In April, the head teacher made a new rule.
After a month, Mr Das filled only half a sack a week.
questions.evidence: Steel bottles are the best answer to litter.
questions.explain: Best is a signal word, and others might suggest a different answer to litter. The other two sentences report things that can be checked.
questions.hint: Look for a signal word such as best or should.

passages.title: Saturday Market
passages.text:
Every Saturday, Latha helps her mother at their vegetable stall. They leave home at five in the morning, before the sun is up. Latha's job is to stack the tomatoes and write the prices on a small board.

Last Saturday it rained heavily. Very few people came to the market. By noon, the baskets were still full, and Latha's mother kept counting the few coins in her tin.

Then Latha tore a page from her notebook. She wrote 'Two kilos for the price of one' in big letters and held it up at the roadside. Soon a line of people stood at the stall. By two o'clock every basket was empty. Her mother hugged her tightly. I think Latha should get a stall of her own one day.

questions.prompt: At what time were the baskets empty?
questions.right: two o'clock
wrong: noon
five in the morning
questions.evidence: By two o'clock every basket was empty.
questions.explain: 'By two o'clock every basket was empty.' At noon the baskets were still full, and five in the morning is when they leave home.
questions.hint: The text has three times. Which one is in the sentence about empty baskets?

questions.prompt: What happened after Latha held up her sign?
questions.right: A line of people stood at the stall.
wrong: It began to rain heavily.
Latha stacked the tomatoes and wrote the prices.
questions.evidence: Soon a line of people stood at the stall.
questions.explain: After she held up the sign, 'Soon a line of people stood at the stall.' The rain and the stacking came before the sign.
questions.hint: Find the sentence where she holds up the page. The next one begins with Soon.

questions.prompt: Why did very few people come to the market?
questions.right: It rained heavily.
wrong: The prices were too high.
The stall opened late.
questions.evidence: Last Saturday it rained heavily.
questions.explain: 'Last Saturday it rained heavily. Very few people came to the market.' The rain is the cause, though the text does not say because.
questions.hint: Read the sentence just before 'Very few people came to the market.'

questions.prompt: Why did Latha write the sign?
questions.right: She wanted to sell the vegetables that were left.
wrong: She wanted to practise writing in big, neat letters.
Her mother told her to.
questions.evidence: By noon, the baskets were still full
questions.explain: The baskets were still full and her mother was counting a few coins. The sign offered a bargain to bring buyers, so Latha wanted to sell what was left.
questions.hint: What was the problem at noon? What does the sign offer to people?

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the last paragraph?
questions.right: Latha's idea brought customers and sold everything.
wrong: Latha tore a page out of her school notebook.
It rained heavily on Saturday and few people came.
questions.evidence: By two o'clock every basket was empty.
questions.explain: The paragraph tells of the sign, the line of people and the empty baskets: her idea worked. Tearing the page is one small step.
questions.hint: Which answer covers the sign, the line of people and the empty baskets together?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: I think Latha should get a stall of her own one day.
wrong: By two o'clock every basket was empty.
Last Saturday it rained heavily.
questions.evidence: I think Latha should get a stall of her own one day.
questions.explain: I think and should are signal words. It is what the writer believes. The other two can be checked.
questions.hint: Find the sentence with I think or should.

passages.title: The Night Train
passages.text:
Imran and his grandfather took the night train from Chennai to Madurai. The train left at half past nine. Imran had the top bed, and his grandfather slept below.

Around midnight, the train stopped at a small station. A man sold hot milk through the window. Imran bought two cups. Next, he climbed down and woke his grandfather gently. They drank the milk together and watched the lamps of the station slide away.

In the morning, Imran found that his grandfather had covered him with his own shawl. The old man sat by the window, rubbing his cold arms and smiling. Night trains are the best way to travel. I think everyone should try one.

questions.prompt: When did the train leave?
questions.right: at half past nine
wrong: around midnight
in the morning
questions.evidence: The train left at half past nine.
questions.explain: 'The train left at half past nine.' Midnight is when it stopped at a small station.

questions.prompt: What did Imran do after he bought the two cups of milk?
questions.right: He climbed down and woke his grandfather.
wrong: He went back to sleep on the top bed.
He covered his grandfather with his own shawl.
questions.evidence: Next, he climbed down and woke his grandfather gently.
questions.explain: The word Next shows it: he climbed down and woke his grandfather.

questions.prompt: Why were the grandfather's arms cold in the morning?
questions.right: He had given his shawl to Imran.
wrong: The train window was broken and let the wind in.
He had spilled the milk.
questions.evidence: his grandfather had covered him with his own shawl
questions.explain: He had covered Imran with his own shawl, so he had nothing warm for himself. The text gives the two facts in different sentences.

questions.prompt: Why did Imran wake his grandfather?
questions.right: To share the hot milk with him.
wrong: To ask him for money.
Because the train had reached Madurai.
questions.evidence: They drank the milk together
questions.explain: He bought two cups, woke his grandfather, and they drank the milk together. He wanted to share it.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the second paragraph?
questions.right: Imran and his grandfather shared hot milk at a midnight stop.
wrong: A man at a small station sold hot milk through the train window.
The train left at half past nine.
questions.evidence: They drank the milk together
questions.explain: The paragraph is about the midnight stop and the two of them sharing milk. The seller is one detail, and the leaving time is in another paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Night trains are the best way to travel.
wrong: The train left at half past nine.
A man sold hot milk through the window.
questions.evidence: Night trains are the best way to travel.
questions.explain: Best is a signal word, and many people prefer other ways to travel. The other two sentences can be checked.

passages.title: The Bird Count
passages.text:
Each January, the children of Kovai Nature Club count the birds at the lake near their town. They meet at six in the morning, when the birds are busiest. Each child carries a notebook and a pencil.

This year, Divya spotted a painted stork first. After that, the group counted ducks for almost an hour. Finally, they added up their lists under a banyan tree. They had seen thirty-two kinds of birds, eight more than last year.

The club leader said the lake was cleaner now. Last March, people from the town had removed the weeds and rubbish from the water. More fish live in clean water, and birds come where the fish are. Bird counting is the best hobby for children. I think schools should take every class to the lake.

questions.prompt: How many kinds of birds did the club see this year?
questions.right: thirty-two
wrong: eight
six
questions.evidence: They had seen thirty-two kinds of birds
questions.explain: 'They had seen thirty-two kinds of birds.' Eight is how many more than last year, and six is the time they meet.

questions.prompt: What did the group do last?
questions.right: They added up their lists under a banyan tree.
wrong: They counted ducks on the water for almost an hour.
They spotted a painted stork.
questions.evidence: Finally, they added up their lists under a banyan tree.
questions.explain: First the stork, after that the ducks, and finally the lists were added up.

questions.prompt: Why did more kinds of birds come to the lake this year?
questions.right: The lake had been cleaned, so more fish live in it.
wrong: The children brought food for the birds every morning.
It rained more in January.
questions.evidence: More fish live in clean water, and birds come where the fish are.
questions.explain: The town cleaned the lake. Clean water holds more fish, and birds come where the fish are.

questions.prompt: Why does each child carry a notebook and a pencil?
questions.right: To write down the birds they see.
wrong: To draw the lake for an art class.
To do homework while they wait.
questions.evidence: Finally, they added up their lists under a banyan tree.
questions.explain: They count birds and later add up their lists, so the notebooks are for writing down the birds they see.
evidenceAlternatives: Each child carries a notebook and a pencil.
Finally, they added up their lists under a banyan tree.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the second paragraph?
questions.right: The group counted the birds and found more kinds than last year.
wrong: Divya saw a painted stork.
There is a banyan tree near the lake where the club meets each January.
questions.evidence: They had seen thirty-two kinds of birds, eight more than last year.
questions.explain: The paragraph follows the count from the first bird to the total. The stork and the tree are details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Bird counting is the best hobby for children.
wrong: Each child carries a notebook and a pencil.
They meet at six in the morning, when the birds are busiest.
questions.evidence: Bird counting is the best hobby for children.
questions.explain: Best is a signal word and people can disagree about hobbies. The other two can be checked.

passages.title: The Broken Window
passages.text:
On Tuesday afternoon, Joseph and his friends were playing cricket in the lane. Joseph hit the ball hard. It flew over the wall and broke Mrs Pillai's kitchen window.

The other boys ran away at once. Joseph stood still for a minute. Then he walked to Mrs Pillai's door and rang the bell. He told her what had happened and said he would pay for the glass from his savings.

Mrs Pillai did not shout. First she swept up the glass. Then she gave Joseph a glass of buttermilk. The next day she told his mother that he was the most honest boy in the lane. Later that week, Joseph gave her sixty rupees. I think children should always own up. Honesty is the best gift.

questions.prompt: When was the window broken?
questions.right: on Tuesday afternoon
wrong: the next day
later that week
questions.evidence: On Tuesday afternoon
questions.explain: The first paragraph begins 'On Tuesday afternoon'. The next day and later that week are about what happened afterwards.

questions.prompt: What did Mrs Pillai do first, after Joseph told her?
questions.right: She swept up the glass.
wrong: She gave Joseph buttermilk.
She spoke to his mother.
questions.evidence: First she swept up the glass.
questions.explain: 'First she swept up the glass. Then she gave Joseph a glass of buttermilk.' She spoke to his mother the next day.

questions.prompt: Why did the window break?
questions.right: Joseph's ball flew over the wall and hit it.
wrong: Mrs Pillai slammed it shut.
The other boys threw stones at it from the lane.
questions.evidence: It flew over the wall and broke Mrs Pillai's kitchen window.
questions.explain: Joseph hit the ball hard, and it flew over the wall and broke the window.

questions.prompt: Why did Joseph ring Mrs Pillai's bell?
questions.right: He wanted to tell the truth and put things right.
wrong: He wanted to ask for his ball back before dark.
His friends dared him to.
questions.evidence: He told her what had happened and said he would pay for the glass from his savings.
questions.explain: At the door he told her what had happened and offered to pay. He went to own up, not to get his ball.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the second paragraph?
questions.right: Joseph owned up when his friends ran away.
wrong: Joseph has some savings.
The boys were playing cricket in the lane on Tuesday.
questions.evidence: He told her what had happened and said he would pay for the glass from his savings.
questions.explain: The paragraph sets the boys who ran against Joseph, who went to the door and told the truth. His savings are a detail.
evidenceAlternatives: The other boys ran away at once.
He told her what had happened and said he would pay for the glass from his savings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Honesty is the best gift.
wrong: Later that week, Joseph gave her sixty rupees.
The other boys ran away at once.
questions.evidence: Honesty is the best gift.
questions.explain: Best is a signal word and it cannot be checked. The other two sentences report what happened.

passages.title: The Science Fair
passages.text:
Nila and Rekha wanted to build a model windmill for the science fair. They had only one week. On the first day, they collected cardboard, a pencil and a small motor from an old toy.

On Wednesday, the blades would not turn. Rekha wanted to give up and make a poster instead. Nila took the model home. She cut the blades again, thinner this time, and tested them in front of the table fan until midnight.

On Friday morning, the windmill turned and lit a tiny bulb. The judges stopped at their table for ten minutes. In the evening, the girls carried home a silver cup. Science fairs are the most exciting school events. I think every child should build something.

questions.prompt: Where did the motor come from?
questions.right: an old toy
wrong: a table fan
the science fair
questions.evidence: a small motor from an old toy
questions.explain: They collected 'a small motor from an old toy'. The table fan was only used for testing the blades.

questions.prompt: What happened on Wednesday?
questions.right: The blades would not turn.
wrong: The girls collected cardboard.
The girls won a silver cup.
questions.evidence: On Wednesday, the blades would not turn.
questions.explain: 'On Wednesday, the blades would not turn.' Collecting was on the first day and the cup came on Friday evening.

questions.prompt: Why did the windmill turn on Friday?
questions.right: Nila had cut the blades thinner.
wrong: The judges repaired it before the fair opened.
The girls bought a new motor.
questions.evidence: She cut the blades again, thinner this time
questions.explain: On Wednesday the blades would not turn. Nila cut them thinner and tested them, and on Friday the windmill turned.

questions.prompt: Why did Nila take the model home?
questions.right: She did not want to give up, and wanted to fix it.
wrong: She wanted to keep it for herself.
Rekha told her to make a poster there instead of a model.
questions.evidence: tested them in front of the table fan until midnight
questions.explain: At home she cut the blades again and tested them until midnight. She took it home to keep working on it.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the second paragraph?
questions.right: The model failed, but Nila kept working on it.
wrong: Nila has a table fan at home that runs until midnight.
Rekha likes making posters.
questions.evidence: She cut the blades again, thinner this time, and tested them in front of the table fan until midnight.
questions.explain: The paragraph tells of the failure and of Nila's work to fix it. The fan and the poster are details.
evidenceAlternatives: On Wednesday, the blades would not turn.
She cut the blades again, thinner this time, and tested them in front of the table fan until midnight.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Science fairs are the most exciting school events.
wrong: They had only one week.
The judges stopped at their table for ten minutes.
questions.evidence: Science fairs are the most exciting school events.
questions.explain: Most exciting is a signal phrase and people can disagree. The other two can be checked.
